fix(project): the conflict scanner reads where surfaces keep their rules (S22)

The file carrying this fix contained a comment predicting the bug:

> A conflict detector that only looks at the filenames it was written for will quietly
> miss a whole rule surface added later.

It then missed one. `.cursor/rules/` had been added once, on the strength of one
estate repository; `.claude/rules/` and `.agents/rules/` were added to `SURFACES`
afterwards and the scan list was not. Two of five surfaces were unscanned, both
of them surfaces that read a rule this tool writes. No repository in the estate
has a hand-written rule in either directory, which is why nothing reported it.

A comment saying "derive this" is not deriving it. The scan list now comes from
`SURFACES` and `POINTERS`, so a surface is scanned from the moment it exists:

- **`GEMINI.md`** — the Antigravity pointer target, this tool's own output, never
  scanned. `CLAUDE.md` was, by hand, for the whole life of the tool; the only
  difference between the two was which was added first.
- **`.claude/rules/` and `.agents/rules/`** — added, at last.
- **The extension is the final segment of the template, not the tail after
  `{name}`.** Copilot writes `{name}.instructions.md`, so matching that suffix
  would be *narrower* than the `.md` that was listed by hand — the difference
  between seeing a hand-written `reviewer.md` in that directory and reporting the
  directory empty. A file this tool writes always carries its suffix; a file a
  person wrote need not, and the person is who this scanner is for.

`ruleGlobs(surfaces = SURFACES)` takes its list as an argument so the derivation
can be shown on a surface this package has never heard of. The default is the one
authority, so no caller can narrow a scan in production.

Four tests. The strongest is that a contradiction planted in all four rule
directories is *found*, not merely listed — a scanner that collects a path and
never reads it reports exactly what one that finds nothing reports. Three
mutations, each failing on the assertion written for it: the hand-written list
back, `GEMINI.md` excluded, the extension taken as the whole tail. 791/791.

The rest of S22 is not here: `nearMatches` gives distance 0 to any substring,
`surfaceProblems` is computed and consumed by nothing, `hooks install` leaves a
shim behind for an event that no longer declares gates, and a staged formatter
passes every file on one argv.
